extractionCharter.objective: Extract operator-facing product context from the Decision OS Context card, then synthesize it into human-readable report data.
inclusionRules: Include only facts stated in the source card.
Prioritize purpose, capabilities, workspace shape, surfaces, controls, workflows, and usable constraints.
Keep source references for extracted items.
exclusionRules: Do not import adjacent repo knowledge.
Do not lead with implementation internals unless they explain an operator-visible feature.
Do not include caveats unless they affect how the operator uses the product.

featureRegister.statement: Decision OS is a local browser canvas for working with decision ledgers in a repo-local workspace.
The main workspace is a full-canvas ledger surface with pan, zoom, route mode, active ledger, viewport, and zoom/detail states.
The product exposes route-addressed ledger tabs and a ledgers overview canvas.
Operators work with cards, zones, groups, relationships, selection, clipboard copy/paste, and card resizing.
Operators can inspect and edit ledgers, create or move canvas objects, review evidence, and maintain summaries.
Cards can contain Markdown, fields, image carousels, HTML card assets, media, and report or mockup material.
The right-side thread inspector contains the terminal-style composer, note history, upload flow, and voice dock.
Threads support pasted images and files, voice notes, transcription retry, and agent treatment of unanswered notes.
The keyboard contract includes A, X, Esc, Del, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, and Ctrl+D.
A normal journey starts by opening a ledger route, reviewing the canvas, selecting or creating objects, editing, then using the thread panel.
Operator notes hand work to agents through thread files, and replies return through agent notes and durable card edits.
The operator owns decisions, notes, approvals, and workspace intent.
The watcher concept monitors unanswered notes.
The interface includes toolbox controls, canvas controls, card detail and overview layers, tab registry, relationship overlays, labels, modals, and status copy.

Visible states include selection, grouped selection, open card tab, low-detail rendering, thread open or closed, draft restored, voice recording, transcription upload, failure, retry, modal open, and external refresh.

Primary entry points include /, /ledgers, /<ledgerId>, the tab registry, card and zone controls, the toolbox, keyboard shortcuts, thread buttons, voice controls, ledger-cli, and server launch commands.
Expensive card detail is hydrated only when detail is visible.
Pan, zoom, and drag must preserve responsive frame production.
Delete actions require confirmation, and thread or voice tooling must not steal editing keystrokes.
Media dimensions persist independent of canvas zoom.
The workspace separates Specs, Data, Performances, and Tasks System; cards, zones, groups, relationships, and threads are the main navigable units.
Live refresh allows external filesystem edits to hand off to the client through server-sent refresh events.

humanReport.title: Decision OS Operator Context
humanReport.subtitle: A source-bound view of what the workspace is for, what operators can do, and how the product is controlled.

openingSnapshot.title: What this is for
bullets: **Decision OS** is a local browser canvas for decision and ledger work.
The workspace is built around `cards`, `zones`, `groups`, `relationships`, and `threads`.
Operators use it to inspect ledgers, edit canvas objects, review evidence, and capture notes.
The active workspace separates `Specs`, `Data`, `Performances`, and `Tasks System`.

sections.title: Workspace Shape
sections.readerQuestion: How should an operator imagine the product?

blocks.title: Canvas first
bullets: **The main workspace is a canvas**, not a linear document.
Operators navigate it with `pan`, `zoom`, active ledger state, and viewport state.
The canvas contains cards, zones, groups, relationships, labels, and overlays.
Detail changes with zoom through low-detail and hydrated card states.

sections.title: What Operators Can Do
sections.readerQuestion: What actions does the product support?

blocks.title: Canvas work
bullets: Open a `ledger` route and review the canvas.
Create, move, select, resize, copy, paste, and delete canvas objects.
Arrange work with `cards`, `zones`, `groups`, and `relationships`.
Review specs, performance evidence, reports, and mockups.

blocks.title: Content work
bullets: Edit card descriptions, fields, and Markdown content.
Inspect image carousels, HTML assets, media, and report cards.
Paste files or images into threads.
Record voice notes and retry transcription when needed.

blocks.title: Visible areas
bullets: The `tab registry` and ledger routes choose the active workspace.
The full-canvas ledger surface holds the spatial work map.
The card detail layer shows descriptions, fields, Markdown, and media.
The right-side thread inspector holds notes, uploads, and voice flow.

blocks.title: Control areas
bullets: The toolbox and canvas controls support editing and navigation.
Relationship overlays show links between objects.
Deletion confirmation modals protect destructive actions.
Telemetry and status copy expose local runtime feedback.

sections.title: Controls That Matter
sections.readerQuestion: Which controls should an operator know first?

blocks.title: Keyboard contract
bullets: `A` opens or focuses the thread panel.
`X` starts or stops the active voice note.
`Esc` cancels capture, closes tooling, or clears selection.
`Del`, `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+V`, and `Ctrl+D` handle deletion, copy, paste, and resize.

sections.title: Workflows
sections.readerQuestion: How does work move through the product?

blocks.title: Operator loop
bullets: Open a ledger route, then review the canvas.
Select or create cards, zones, or groups.
Edit geometry or content, then open the thread panel.
Write or record notes, then review replies, media, reports, or mockups.

blocks.title: Handoffs
bullets: Operator notes hand work to agents through thread files.
Voice capture moves through recording, upload, transcription, note update, and retry.
External filesystem edits refresh visible ledger content through server-sent events.
Card Markdown moves through hydration and frontend rendering.

blocks.title: Interaction rules
bullets: Rich card detail appears only when detail is visible.
Pan, zoom, and drag must stay responsive.
Delete actions require confirmation.
Thread and voice tooling must not steal editing keystrokes.

blocks.title: Content rules
bullets: Media dimensions persist independently from canvas zoom.
HTML embeds must stay under allowed card asset paths.
Agent replies must be in English.
Durable card content should stay concrete and traceable.

evidenceIndex.claim: Decision OS is a local browser canvas with workspace-local data.
The surface includes ledger tabs, canvas, objects, pan/zoom, Markdown, media, HTML assets, threads, voice, and CLI tools.
Operators inspect/edit ledgers, manipulate canvas objects, review evidence, paste media, record voice, treat notes, maintain summaries, and use report cards.
The UX includes tab registry, full-canvas ledger surface, toolbox, canvas controls, card layers, overlays, labels, modals, thread inspector, composer, voice dock, and status copy.
The implemented keyboard contract includes A, X, Esc, Del, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, and Ctrl+D.
Interaction constraints include detail hydration, responsive pan/zoom/drag, deletion confirmation, editing key protection, media sizing, and HTML asset paths.
